project.name: SMART CITY SITE PLANNING
project.subtitle: Sustainable Urban Development Through Intelligent Site Design.
project.abstract: An integrated urban planning initiative exploring sustainable land utilization, environmental performance, intelligent transportation, green infrastructure, and resilient urban development using Autodesk Forma and Revit.
objectives: Develop an intelligent, data-driven site plan covering a minimum area of 1.0 km² using Autodesk Forma Site Design.
Execute multi-disciplinary environmental analyses: Sun Hours, Daylight Potential, Wind Dynamics, UTCI Microclimate, Embodied Carbon, Noise, and Solar Yield.
Conduct a rigorous Forma Board comparative evaluation between multiple distinct design proposals.
Establish an interoperable BIM pipeline exporting Forma site geometry into Autodesk Revit for architectural drawing block development.
Deliver resilient urban infrastructure prioritizing transit-oriented development, sustainable water management, and biophilic corridors.
project.noAiDeclaration: Original work made in Autodesk Forma - no AI-generated content.

workflowSteps.description: Delimitation of a 1.28 km² urban boundary with GIS elevation and satellite boundary import.

workflowSteps.name: Context Research
workflowSteps.description: Assessment of microclimatic conditions, solar path, prevailing wind rose, and existing surrounding roads.

workflowSteps.name: Generative Design
workflowSteps.description: Formulation of Proposal A (Biophilic TOD Core) and Proposal B (Polycentric Superblocks).

workflowSteps.name: Multi-Factor Analysis
workflowSteps.description: Rigorous execution of the 8 Forma analysis modules including embodied carbon, daylight, and wind comfort.

workflowSteps.name: Forma Board Comparison
workflowSteps.description: Side-by-side metric normalization, multi-criteria trade-off scoring, and final selection.

workflowSteps.name: Revit Export & BIM

site.name: Sector 14 Urban Growth Corridor
site.zoning: High-Density Mixed-Use Commercial / Residential (Smart City Special Zone)
site.terrainDescription: Gently undulating alluvial plain with natural southwest drainage incline (average elevation 81m above MSL).

context.terrain: Topographic slope of 1.4% toward the Sabarmati drainage sub-basin, optimal for gravity-assisted stormwater harvesting.
context.existingBuildings: Low-rise peri-urban settlements along northern boundary; light industrial buffer on the eastern perimeter.
context.roads: Connected to NH48 via 45m arterial corridor on southern edge and 24m collector grid.
context.climate: Hot dry summers with peak temperatures exceeding 42°C, moderate monsoon (650mm annual rainfall), mild winter.
context.nearbyInfrastructure: Proposed metro feeder station within 800m; 66kV electrical substation adjacent to east parcel.
context.greenSpaces: Existing riparian buffer strip along western boundary preserved as continuous ecological corridor.

mandatoryElements.title: Site Limits
mandatoryElements.description: Precisely delineated 1.28 km² site boundary exceeding the 1.0 km² minimum site planning threshold. Georeferenced in EPSG:4326 with full setback offsets.

mandatoryElements.title: Landscaping & Green Infrastructure
mandatoryElements.description: Urban forest belt, sponge city rain bioswales, pedestrian shade canopy, and 34% active permeable green cover in the selected proposal.

mandatoryElements.title: Buildings & Massing
mandatoryElements.description: Iterative building massing optimized in Forma for daylight penetration and natural ventilation, transitioning from 14-story central towers to 4-story perimeter blocks.

mandatoryElements.title: Transportation & Mobility
mandatoryElements.description: Multi-tier transit network: Dedicated EV bus rapid lane, grade-separated cycle highways, 15-minute walkable residential quadrants, and peripheral park-and-ride hubs.

proposals.name: Proposal A: Biophilic Transit-Oriented Core
proposals.tagline: High-density pedestrian core wrapped around an active ecological park corridor
proposals.description: Proposal A consolidates highest building densities immediately adjacent to the transit artery, creating high floor-area-ratio (FAR 3.2) while preserving 34% contiguous ground green space. Stepped building profiles optimize solar access.
proposals.designPhilosophy: Biophilic density — maximizing human walkable encounters while channeling cooling regional winds through open green fingers.
proposals.planningStrategy: Centralized high-density core with 5-minute transit walks, progressive height stepping away from prevailing wind vectors.
proposals.siteUtilization: Compact core footprint leaving vast interconnected open parks and stormwater percolation zones.
proposals.transportationHighlights: 100% segregated bicycle lanes, 3 EV micro-mobility hubs, central pedestrian boulevard.
proposals.teamNotes: Achieved 18% lower embodied carbon than baseline through optimized volume-to-envelope ratios and engineered timber podium structures.

proposals.name: Proposal B: Polycentric Microclimate Superblocks
proposals.tagline: Distributed mid-rise clusters engineered for localized wind tunneling and solar self-sufficiency
proposals.description: Proposal B disperses built mass into four semi-autonomous courtyard superblocks (FAR 2.4). Each superblock features inward-facing microclimate courtyards that capture seasonal cooling breezes.
proposals.designPhilosophy: Vernacular climatic adaptation scaled to urban superblocks — creating micro-scale heat sinks across the district.
proposals.planningStrategy: Decentralized amenities within each 400m block, perimeter street walls shielding inner courtyards from external traffic noise.
proposals.siteUtilization: Evenly distributed medium-density footprint with pocket parks embedded inside each superblock quadrant.
proposals.transportationHighlights: Ring road access with restricted interior shared streets (Woonerf concept), underground parking.
proposals.teamNotes: Excels in daylight uniformity across all units, but incurs higher building envelope area resulting in marginally higher embodied carbon.

area-metrics.title: Area Metrics & Density
area-metrics.whatItMeasures: Gross Floor Area (GFA), Building Footprint, Site Coverage Ratio, and Floor Area Ratio (FAR) evaluated against municipal master plan zoning limits.
area-metrics.proposalAResults: GFA: 412,000 m² | Footprint: 142,000 m² | FAR: 3.22 | Ground Coverage: 28.4%
area-metrics.proposalBResults: GFA: 338,000 m² | Footprint: 178,000 m² | FAR: 2.64 | Ground Coverage: 35.6%
area-metrics.keyInsight: Proposal A achieves 21.9% higher usable space efficiency with a 20.2% smaller ground footprint, preserving crucial contiguous ground space for retention basins.

embodied-carbon.title: Embodied Carbon Analysis
embodied-carbon.whatItMeasures: Estimated cradle-to-gate upfront embodied greenhouse gas emissions per square meter of gross floor area (kg CO₂e/m²) calculated via Forma Embodied Carbon Beta.
embodied-carbon.proposalAResults: 385 kg CO₂e/m² (Total: ~158,620 t CO₂e across development lifecycle)
embodied-carbon.proposalBResults: 432 kg CO₂e/m² (Total: ~146,016 t CO₂e across development lifecycle)
embodied-carbon.keyInsight: Proposal A delivers a 10.9% lower carbon intensity per unit floor area owing to efficient compact massing, reduced exterior surface-to-volume ratio, and shared core geometries.

sun-hours.title: Sun Hours Analysis
sun-hours.whatItMeasures: Direct sunlight hours received on ground surfaces, public plazas, and building facades during critical equinox (March 21) and summer solstice (June 21).
sun-hours.proposalAResults: Public parks average 5.4 hours direct sun; deep street canyons shaded during peak noon hours (11:00 - 14:00).
sun-hours.proposalBResults: Central courtyards average 6.1 hours direct sun; perimeter blocks experience higher direct heat load.
sun-hours.keyInsight: Proposal A utilizes targeted building orientation (azimuth 15° west of south) to deliberately cast shade over major pedestrian walkways during peak heat hours.

daylight-potential.title: Daylight Potential
daylight-potential.whatItMeasures: Percentage of internal occupied floor plate receiving adequate natural daylight (Daylight Factor ≥ 2.0% or Spatial Daylight Autonomy sDA 300/50% > 55%).
daylight-potential.proposalAResults: 74.8% of gross residential and commercial floor area meets optimal daylighting criteria.
daylight-potential.proposalBResults: 81.2% of occupied floor area meets daylight criteria due to narrower building depths.
daylight-potential.keyInsight: Proposal B edges ahead in daylight penetration (81.2% vs 74.8%) due to shallow courtyard building depths (14m vs 18m). Both comfortably exceed LEED minimum thresholds.

wind-analysis.title: Wind Comfort & Aerodynamics
wind-analysis.whatItMeasures: Pedestrian-level wind comfort using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) under Lawson Criteria (Sitting, Standing, Strolling, Uncomfortable) driven by prevailing SW summer winds.
wind-analysis.proposalAResults: 88% of pedestrian zones classified as 'Comfortable for Sitting/Standing' (0.5 - 2.8 m/s); zero dangerous downwash vortex spots.
wind-analysis.proposalBResults: 79% comfortable; minor corner acceleration (>5.2 m/s) noted at northeast superblock edge.
wind-analysis.keyInsight: Proposal A's tiered building heights induce boundary layer deceleration, capturing cooling summer breezes at upper levels while maintaining gentle air exchange at the ground.

microclimate.title: Microclimate & Thermal Comfort
microclimate.whatItMeasures: Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) perceived outdoor temperature combining solar radiation, wind speed, relative humidity, and surface emissivity.
microclimate.proposalAResults: Peak summer perceived temperature reduced by 3.2°C in shaded green corridors compared to bare urban baseline.
microclimate.proposalBResults: Peak summer perceived temperature reduced by 2.1°C; central courtyards function as moderate nocturnal heat traps.
microclimate.keyInsight: The continuous canopy and bioswale network of Proposal A produces a localized microclimate cooling effect, extending outdoor pedestrian comfort by an estimated 4.5 hours daily.

noise-analysis.title: Noise Analysis & Acoustic Comfort
noise-analysis.whatItMeasures: Traffic and urban noise propagation in dBA from the southern arterial road across residential facades and public open recreational spaces.
noise-analysis.proposalAResults: Residential interior buffer zones maintain 48.5 dBA average; acoustic earth berm and commercial podium block arterial noise.
noise-analysis.proposalBResults: 52.1 dBA average; reflection off hard courtyard facades elevates interior reverberation slightly.
noise-analysis.keyInsight: Proposal A shields 92% of residential units below the CPCB recommended daytime residential ambient limit of 55 dBA through strategic commercial frontage buffering.

solar-energy.title: Solar Energy & PV Potential
solar-energy.whatItMeasures: Annual incident solar radiation (kWh/m²/year) on usable rooftop and building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) facade surfaces for clean on-site power generation.
solar-energy.proposalAResults: 1,420 kWh/m²/year rooftop yield; potential generation of ~18.4 GWh/year supplying 36% of total operational demand.
solar-energy.proposalBResults: 1,580 kWh/m²/year rooftop yield; potential generation of ~21.2 GWh/year supplying 43% of total operational demand.
solar-energy.keyInsight: Proposal B provides 15.2% higher total solar PV collection area due to wider rooftop footprints, making it exceptionally well-suited for decentralized net-zero electrical grids.

comparison.teamDecision: Proposal A (Biophilic Transit-Oriented Core) is selected as the primary design scheme for detailed Autodesk Revit BIM development.
comparison.teamJustification: While Proposal B delivers higher solar insolation, Proposal A achieves superior multi-factor equilibrium: 34.2% contiguous green space (+5.7%), 10.9% lower embodied carbon intensity, exceptional pedestrian wind comfort (88/100), and an integrated 15-minute transit-oriented spine that significantly reduces private vehicle dependence.
comparison.scoringDisclaimer: The weighted score is a team decision-support tool and does not replace engineering judgment or the official Autodesk Forma Board evaluation.

smartCityFeatures.title: Grade-Separated Active Mobility Network
smartCityFeatures.description: Continuous 8.4 km network of grade-separated cycle highways and pedestrian greenways connecting all residential quadrants directly to the central transit terminal.

smartCityFeatures.title: Smart EV Autonomous Shuttle Spine
smartCityFeatures.description: Dedicated median transit right-of-way reserved exclusively for zero-emission autonomous feeder shuttles operating on demand-responsive schedules.

smartCityFeatures.title: Sponge City Urban Drainage Corridor
smartCityFeatures.description: Engineered bioswales, retention wetlands, and permeable pavements sized to absorb 100-year storm events while recharging groundwater aquifers.

smartCityFeatures.title: District Microgrid with Rooftop Solar PV
smartCityFeatures.description: Smart bidirectional electrical microgrid coordinating 18.4 GWh annual rooftop solar yield with centralized battery energy storage (BESS).

smartCityFeatures.title: Decentralized Greywater Reclamation
smartCityFeatures.description: Closed-loop biological wastewater treatment plant recycling 85% of domestic greywater for landscape irrigation and district cooling towers.

smartCityFeatures.title: Wind Funneling & Microclimate Cooling
smartCityFeatures.description: Aerodynamically stepped building massing designed in Forma to scoop southwest summer winds through vegetative misting zones.

smartCityFeatures.title: Multi-Hazard Emergency Access Grid
smartCityFeatures.description: Dual-ring arterial connectivity guaranteeing emergency vehicle response times under 4 minutes to any quadrant, even during flash inundation.
